senses.gloss:
Duhitṛ is the regular designation of ‘daughter’ from the Rigveda onwards. The word appears to be derived from duh, ‘milk,’ in the sense of one who nourishes a child, rather than as the ‘milker’ of the primitive family or the suckling. See also strī, pati, pitṛ, bhrātṛ.
Foot notes Rv. viii. 101, 15; x. 17, 1; 40, 5; 61, 5, 7; Av. ii. 14, 2; vi. 100, 3; vii. 12, 1; x. 1, 25; Śatapatha brāhmaṇa, i. 7, 4, 1; 8, 1, 8, etc.
Delbrück, Dic indogermanischen Verwandtschaftsnamen, 454.
